history: Found as a three-way split: Python and Rust refused at the decoder, the npm CLI and the verify page both substituted U+FFFD and verified the result. The npm half is closed. The browser half is OPEN.
note: The collision half of 008, and the reason it matters. These bytes are a different file from 008's -- 0x80 rather than 0xFF, and 0xC3 is a third -- and all three decode to the same U+FFFD in the browser, canonicalise to the same bytes, and produce the SAME receipt_sha256 (c856f23670aa3692..). A canonical form exists so that distinct documents have distinct bytes; canonical.py says exactly this about allow_nan, that permitting NaN 'would let two different receipts share a canonical form'. Silent U+FFFD substitution lets them, and it happens before any verifier code runs. TextDecoder takes {fatal: true}.
